A1.justification: Both PDFs describe AdaSteer. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices are readable and support reliable matching of retained, revised, and added material.

before.justification: Section 4 and Appendix D report original jailbreak-defense, utility, over-safety, ablation, model-size, and inference-efficiency results.

after.justification: v2 retains these empirical results and adds a Gemma-2-27B evaluation in Appendix D.4 and Table 4.

M1.justification: Section 3 retains the same direction construction, vector projection, adaptive coefficients, and activation-steering procedure in Equations 1–11. The calibration explanations do not establish an algorithm revision, and Appendix E.2 presents fine-tuning with an MSE loss as future work.

E1.justification: The direction-identification datasets, seven jailbreak attack families, XSTest, OKTest, and AlpacaEval are retained. Gemma-2-27B adds a model configuration rather than new dataset or task coverage. The new multilingual discussion introduces no additional languages or test scenarios.

E2.justification: Corresponding comparisons retain ROSE, Self-CD, Jailbreak Antidote, Surgical, InferAligner, and CAST. The added Gemma-2-27B experiment compares AdaSteer with the unmodified backbone, following the existing model-size analysis; no new defense comparator is introduced.

E3.justification: Appendix A.2 changes the stated AdvBench query counts from 100 to 25 for Cipher and from 100 to 50 for GCG. Section 4.6 replaces relative inference time with tokens per second. v2 also adds the 27B configuration and changes Qwen2.5's b_c from 2.7 to 3.0 in Table 10. These revise settings within the retained evaluation design without establishing which existing experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: Appendix D.4 extends the existing model-size analysis with Gemma-2-27B, testing scalability beyond the previous 14B maximum. The steering-vector ablations and baseline hyperparameter sweeps remain. The new multilingual and limited-data discussions do not introduce corresponding new ablation experiments.

E5.justification: Both versions report point estimates without repeated-run counts, seed information, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. The newly disclosed calibration sample count is not uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: New Table 4 reports Gemma-2-27B DSRs of 27.86% without AdaSteer and 92.57% with it, plus a 47.29% utility win rate. Existing entries also change: Table 1's LLaMA multilingual baseline is 67→22, and Qwen Surgical's utility is 47.90→48.85. Detailed XSTest/OKTest results are reassigned under retained headers. These are added results and reporting revisions; the original three backbones' main AdaSteer DSR results remain unchanged.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions, Equations 1–11, and empirical Rejection Law and Harmfulness Law arguments are retained. Appendix E's conceptual discussion adds no formal assumptions, derivations, theorems, or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same adaptive dual-direction defense contribution and claims concerning rejection, harmfulness, safety, utility, and scalability. The added larger-model evidence supports these existing claims without redefining the central contribution.

C2.justification: Appendix E discusses possible fine-tuning toward steered activations, reuse of fixed directions across attacks, and applicability with limited probing data. Appendix D.5 adds interpretation of multilingual performance and acknowledges room for improvement in low-resource languages. The existing linearity and 30B-plus evaluation limitations remain.

D1.justification: v2 adds a code-repository pointer, expands coefficient-calibration instructions, and discloses 158 benign calibration cases for LLaMA-3.1. It updates Qwen2.5's b_c and omits v1's instruction to reverse vHD when positive steering fails to improve compliance. The 15/13/5 probing counts and balanced example groups are retained, partly relocated to Appendix E.3.

R1.justification: v2 adds Zhao et al. (2025), MPO: Multilingual Safety Alignment via Reward Gap Optimization, to the multilingual discussion and references. The principal positioning against prior steering and defense methods remains unchanged; the added linear-representation discussion cites works already present in v1.

P1.justification: v2 makes localized corrections such as A-Law→H-Law and disHD→posHD, partially rewrites Appendix C, and adds Appendix D.5, Appendix E, acknowledgments, and a corresponding-author note. The main section order and most prose remain intact.

P2.justification: Several figures receive localized redraws or styling changes, including a simplified Figure 1 and revised chart formatting. Figure 4 switches to a tokens-per-second axis. v2 adds the Gemma-2-27B table and relocates retained appendix tables and evaluator prompt boxes, while preserving the overall document format.

improvement.justification: The 27B experiment strengthens scalability evidence beyond v1's 14B maximum, while calibration explanations, numerical corrections, and a code-access pointer improve documentation. These are modest gains, tempered by omitted vHD sign-adjustment guidance and remaining inconsistencies: the new Appendix D.5 still cites a 67% LLaMA multilingual baseline although Table 1 now reports 22%.
